public_rationale: The factual-prose limitation has support for the tested biography task: the study available by October 11, 2023, reported supported-fact scores of 42.5% for InstructGPT and 58.3% for ChatGPT [e1]. The broad summarization limitation is contradicted by a September 18, 2023, study: across five tasks, human evaluators preferred LLM summaries to human reference summaries, and the study reported better factual consistency [e2]. The July 6, 2023, long-context study found weaknesses in question answering and retrieval, but did not establish a human competence threshold or test full-book comprehension [e3].
limitations: The biography study lacks a matched human-writing baseline and does not establish inability across all factual writing [e1].
Preference over reference summaries does not establish competence on every summarization task [e2].
Question answering, fact-checking, hostile-witness cross-examination and full-book comprehension remain unsettled by this packet.
The evidence does not establish how many task categories fail a common competence standard or characterize every system available by October 18, 2023.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Existing AI systems cannot competently perform many purely language-based tasks humans can do, such as writing factual prose, summarizing, fact-checking, and understanding a full book.

statement.excerpt: There are many purely language-based tasks that humans can do — question answering, writing factual prose, summarizing, examining the truth of a claim, cross-examining a hostile witness in court, reading and understanding a full-length book — that existing AI systems cannot perform “competently”.
statement.document_title: Reports of the birth of AGI are greatly exaggerated

from_speaker: question answering, writing factual prose, summarizing
examining the truth of a claim
cross-examining a hostile witness in court
reading and understanding a full-length book
our_interpretation: Competence means producing ordinarily usable, substantially correct work on representative tasks, allowing occasional mistakes. It does not require perfection.
The named activities are substantive examples of the asserted limitations. Findings can support some examples while contradicting others.

Existing systems refers to systems available by October 18, 2023. With no reporting cadence specified, the observation window is the current calendar year through the post date; later systems do not count.
Human preference and factual accuracy are relevant measures, but neither alone establishes competence across every version of a task.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evaluations of contemporary systems show substantial reliability failures on several named activities that competent humans can perform. Evidence confined to one activity supports only that part.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporary systems produce reliably usable work comparable to human work on the named activities. Evidence of competence on one activity contradicts its inclusion, without disproving every other limitation.

evidence.explanation: Human checking found substantial unsupported factual content in generated biographies. This supports the factual-prose limitation for the tested systems and task, without establishing that all factual writing was beyond their competence.

evidence.excerpt: better factual consistency and fewer instances of extrinsic hallucinations
evidence.explanation: Across five summarization tasks, human evaluators preferred model summaries to the human references; the factuality comparison also favored GPT-4. This contradicts treating summarization generally as an activity contemporary systems could not perform competently.

The study documents weaknesses in multi-document question answering and retrieval from long inputs. It supplies relevant context but neither tests full-book comprehension nor establishes a human competence threshold.
